result.title: FORGE: Fault-Oriented Rework Code Generation for Executable Interlocking Assembly
result.summary: Large language models have demonstrated strong capabilities in structured reasoning and code generation, yet identifying an assembly fault does not guarantee the ability to generate executable rework programs. In interlocking assemblies, a locally plausible repair program may violate blocking dependencies, omit required recovery operations, or terminate in an incorrect configuration. We identify this challenge as fault-conditioned executable rework generation, where models must jointly reason about structural failures and generate programs that restore constrained assembly states. To benchmark this capability, we introduce FORGE-Bench, containing 4,000 tasks across 26 interlocking assemblies with five assemblies held out for evaluating generalization to unseen structures. We further propose FORGE (Fault-Oriented Rework Code Generation for Executable Interlocking Assembly), a structured state-to-program framework that decomposes rework generation into Rework Structuring and Action Grounding. Rework Structuring captures fault-induced recovery dependencies, while Action Grounding maps these dependencies into state-conditioned executable actions. Experiments show that locally reasonable repair code is insufficient for reliable assembly recovery, and that connecting structural recovery reasoning with executable action realization is essential for verified target restoration.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「故障条件下的可执行返修生成」任务与 FORGE-Bench（4000 个任务、26 个互锁装配体），并给出将返修生成分解为「返修结构化」与「动作落地」的状态到程序框架。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先推理结构恢复依赖、再落地为状态条件化的可执行动作」的两段式分解，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 推理状态与最终答案或动作之间的衔接与可执行性验证，但领域为装配代码生成，无视觉状态输入。
